fixture: Purchased Pisco regulator installed in the printed receiver.
bench_result: The original and older three-diamond covers were loose in A. The matched A cover also rocked. Derek rejected the projections on B and preferred the older three-diamond cover in its previous quadrant.
time_reference: All times are seconds from the start of each original Canon recording. Excerpts preserve original speed and audio.

recordings.configuration: A receiver with the older three-diamond cover.
recordings.bench_observation: Derek installs the cover and shifts it between two positions by fingertip pressure.

testimony.derek: that is incredibly loose, shifting from one position to another

recordings.configuration: B receiver and B cover. The opening shows two long parallel recessed bars on the cover. Derek calls it two diamond aloud.
recordings.bench_observation: Derek points out projections on both sides of the regulator, shows their ends and presses in the cover. He thinks a projection snapped during insertion and rejects these stops. Which feature snapped is unresolved.

testimony.derek: but that just gets in the way. This is impossible to print.
I think one of those snapped, of course.
No, no, I don't think those are a very good idea.

media.view: Matched bars and notches before assembly.
Receiver stop beside the seated regulator before the cover goes on.

recordings.configuration: A receiver with the unmarked original cover.
recordings.bench_observation: Derek seats the original cover, presses opposite sides and demonstrates the movement at the outlet.

recordings.configuration: A receiver with its one-bar A cover.
recordings.bench_observation: The one-bar cover is visible before insertion. Derek alternates fingertip pressure after seating it.

recordings.configuration: Older three-diamond cover in the previous enclosure quadrant.
recordings.bench_observation: Derek tests the cover inside the quadrant, turns the wall toward the camera and manipulates the exposed white outlet. The inside view shows all three diamond marks.

testimony.derek: The one that I said originally had a nice snap to it when it shifts between positions.
It's really the one that feels firmest so far, especially in terms of what it does here.
Consider how this one is still the best so far.

media.view: Source stills, left to right. Outside outlet under hand pressure and inside view of the marked cover.
